source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus publishes 33 MW of IT capacity, ranking sixth among Texas facilities that disclose power figures and representing 6.9% of the state's disclosed 475 MW total.

At common AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this facility would support roughly 825 racks. At 100 kW per rack for GPU-dense inference, it would support roughly 330 racks. The gap between these figures shows how workload type reshapes what a fixed power budget can run. Higher power densities squeeze more compute per megawatt but demand better cooling and electrical distribution. The 175,000 square feet of technical space gives the operator room to choose between density and efficiency.

The six certifications—SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, TIA-942, and HITRUST—mark this as a facility built for regulated enterprise and government workloads rather than consumer-facing AI services. These are not AI-specific credentials. They indicate the campus was architected to house financial systems, health records, and federal data. Whether it now hosts AI workloads or could be repurposed for them is not stated in the operator specification.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities but only 19 publish IT power capacity. This facility is among the nineteen that disclose. The 114-facility gap means the state's actual total capacity is unknown. CyrusOne San Antonio is one of the few operators transparent enough to enable any comparison at all.
